QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r9.claim: Joseph accepted hardship for God over bodily pleasure, and God later favored him over his brothers.
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r9.anchor: لحوق المشقة في الله على لذة نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r11.claim: The brothers swear that God favored Joseph, reversing their earlier denial of his merit; one who truly witnesses does not deny.
QUSHAYRI:v2p90/r11.anchor: من جحد فلأنه ما شهد ، ومن شهد فما جحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r2.claim: Īthār broadly means favor and all kinds of gifts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p316/r2.anchor: الإيثار: لفظ يعم جميع التفضل وأنواع العطايا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God favored Joseph with kingship, patience, and knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r3.anchor: فضلك بالملك، أو بالصبر، والعلم قالهما ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r4.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says God favored Joseph with forbearance and forgiveness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r4.anchor: أو بالحلم والصفح ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari relates God’s favor to piety, patience, and the conduct of the good, matching the preceding verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r5.anchor: قاله: الزمخشري، وهو مناسب لقوله: إنه من يتق الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r6.claim: The brothers’ confession that Joseph was favored also seeks to elicit his kindness and acknowledges their wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r6.anchor: وخطابهم إياه بذلك استنزال لإحسانه، واعتراف بما صدر منهم في حقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r7.claim: Khāṭiʾīn describes deliberate wrongdoing, whereas akhṭaʾ describes aiming at what is right but failing to attain it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p320#2/r7.anchor: وخاطئين: من خطىء إذا تعمد. وأما أخطأ فقصد الصواب ولم يوفق له

NAHHAS:v2p343/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p343/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p343/r3.claim: آثرك means preferred you; its active participle is مؤثر and verbal noun إيثار; خطئين means committing error.
NAHHAS:v2p343/r3.anchor: واسم الفاعل مؤثر والمصدر إيثار ويقال أثرت التراب إثارة

DURR-FULL:v4p577/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r6.claim: Qatadah says Joseph proved gentle: he did not expose or rebuke his brothers for their past acts.
DURR-FULL:v4p577/r6.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا} وذلك بعدما عرفهم نفسه لقوا رجلا حليما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r4.claim: The brothers’ confession that God preferred Joseph is a plea for reconciliation and implicitly admits their guilt; athara covers all forms of preference and gifts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r4.anchor: هذا منهم استنزال ليوسف وإقرار بالذنب في ضمنه استغفار منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r5.claim: Khāṭiʾūn means those who intentionally commit error, unlike mukhṭiʾ, one who aims correctly but misses; Umayya ibn al-Askar supplies a poetic example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p277/r5.anchor: وهو المعتمد للخطأ، والمخطئ من أخطأ، وهو الذي قصد الصواب

MUQATIL:12:91-95/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r1.claim: The brothers admit wrongdoing and say God chose Joseph over them; Muqatil links “we will not choose you” in 20:72 to this sense of choosing.
MUQATIL:12:91-95/r1.anchor: { قالوا تالله } ، يعني والله، { لقد آثرك الله علينا } ، يعني اختارك، كقوله في طه: لن نؤثرك [طه: 72]،

QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r7.claim: The hamza in ātharaka is lightened rather than fully realized; the verb means God preferred Joseph and chose him for knowledge, forbearance, judgment, intellect, and kingship.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r7.anchor: لقد فضلك الله علينا، واختارك بالعلم والحلم والحكم والعقل والملك

QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r8.claim: Asked how the brothers could call themselves sinners despite acting deliberately, Ibn ʿAbbās answers that they knowingly acted but first missed the truth and departed its proper path.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r8.anchor: قال: وإن تعمدوا لذلك، فما تعمدوا حتى أخطؤوا الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r9.claim: Their admission of wrongdoing carries an implicit request for pardon; every sinner has left the path of truth and fallen into doubt and disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:90-92/r9.anchor: وفي ضمن هذا سؤال العفو. وقيل لابن عباس: كيف قالوا «وإن كنا لخاطئين»

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

TABATABAI:12:89-92/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:89-92/r5.claim: Ithar means choosing or preferring, and khatiʾ and mukhtiʾ both denote one who errs; the brothers acknowledge their wrongdoing and God’s preference for Joseph.

TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r5.claim: The brothers admit they sinned and say God favored Yusuf with patience, knowledge, reason, beauty, and kingship; their admission shows remorse rather than persistence.
TABRISI:12:90-92#2/r5.anchor: فضلك واختارك الله علينا بالحلم والعلم والعقل والحسن والملك

THALABI:v5p254/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p254/r1.claim: خاطئين means guilty or sinful; the source gives its verb forms and cites Umayya's verse as evidence.
THALABI:v5p254/r1.anchor: لمخطئين، مذنبين، يقال: خطئ، يخطأ، خطأ وخطأ وأخطأ إذا أذنب

THALABI:v5p254/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r2.speaker: أمية بن الأكسر
THALABI:v5p254/r2.claim: Umayya's line uses خطئا to mean they sinned.
THALABI:v5p254/r2.anchor: قال أمية بن الأكسر: وإن مهاجرين تكنفاه … لعمر الله قد خطئا وخابا

THALABI:v5p254/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p254/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p254/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they missed the truth even though they acted intentionally; every sinner leaves the path of truth for doubt and disobedience.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r3.claim: The brothers acknowledge that God favored Joseph over them with intellect, knowledge, excellence, and beauty, and they admit their wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:90-93/r3.anchor: فضلك الله علينا بالعقل والعلم، والفضل والحسن

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.claim: Joseph identifies himself by recalling what his brothers did to him and Benjamin, fulfilling the revelation that he would later tell them of it when they did not recognize him (12:15).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r1.anchor: Kardeşlerinin yaptıklarını bir gün onlara kendileri (senin kim olduğunun) farkına varmadan mutlaka haber vereceksin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.claim: His brothers admit their wrong and apologize, and Joseph tells them he forgives them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r2.anchor: Kardeşleri kusurlarını itiraf edip özür dilediler. O da onları bağışladığını bildirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.claim: Envy cannot block a blessing God has decreed; the Prophet prayed that no one can withhold what God gives, and the brothers ultimately acknowledge God favored Joseph over them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r3.anchor: İnsanların kıskanması, Allah’ın bir kimse için takdir etmiş olduğu nimeti engelleyemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.claim: The Prophet’s prayer says no one can prevent what God grants, and no one can grant what God withholds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r4.anchor: Senin verdiğine engel olacak yoktur. Senin engel olduğunu da verecek yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.speaker: Ziyâ Paşa
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.claim: Ziya Pasha’s couplet says divine power eventually makes tyrants admit that God favored another over them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:89/r5.anchor: Zalimlere bir gün dedirir kudret-i Mevlâ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The brothers' admission recognizes that their resentment came from their father's preference for Joseph, while God's preference exposed their error and affirmed Joseph's deserving status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God by giving him this preference made them realize their mistake.

BURSEVI:v4p204/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p204/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p204/r3.claim: After recognizing Joseph, the brothers approach the throne intending to fall at his feet; he descends and embraces them.
BURSEVI:v4p204/r3.anchor: ون برادران يوسف را بشناختند روى بتخت آورده خواستند كه دراى وى افتند يوسف ازتخت فروده آمده

BURSEVI:v4p204/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p204/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p204/r4.claim: The brothers admit God favored Joseph in beauty, perfection, status, and wealth, and say they knowingly committed sin.
BURSEVI:v4p204/r4.anchor: اختارك وفضلك علينا بالجمال والكمال والجاه والمال

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r1.claim: Alusi prefers that God's favor meant the brothers were surpassed through piety and patience; other reports explain it by kingship, patience and knowledge, forbearance, or a wider list of virtues and royal power.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r1.anchor: أي اختارك وفضلك علينا بالتقوى والصبر وقيل : بالملك وقيل : بالصبر والعلم ورويا عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r2.speaker: سليمان الدمشقي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r2.claim: Sulayman al-Dimashqi explains God's favor as Joseph's forbearance and forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r2.anchor: وقيل : بالحلم والصفح ذكره سليمان الدمشقي

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r3.speaker: صاحب الغنيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r3.claim: The author of al-Ghunyān lists Joseph's good character and appearance, knowledge, forbearance, beneficence, kingship, patience with their harm, and power as reasons for God's favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب الغنيان : بحسن الخلق والخلق والعلم والحلم والاحسان والملك والسلطان والصبر على أذانا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r4.claim: The brothers admit they were deliberate sinners; the circumstantial conjunction marks their state, إِنّ is lightened with an implicit pronoun of شأن, and the lām in the predicate is the shifted emphatic lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r4.anchor: أي لمتعمدين للذنب إذ فعلنا ما فعلنا ولذلك أعزك وأذلنا فالواو حالية و ( إن ) مخففة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r5.claim: Calling themselves intentional sinners both seeks Joseph's kindness and confesses their wrongdoing with an implicit signal of repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r5.anchor: من الاستنزال لاحسانه عليه السلام والاعتراف بما صدر منهم في حقه مع الاشعار بالتوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r6.claim: خاطئين derives from a verb for intentional sin, unlike أخطأ, which describes aiming at what is right but failing to attain it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p50/r6.anchor: من خطيء إذا تعمد وأما اخطأ فقصد الصواب ولم يوفق له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.claim: The brothers apologize, acknowledging that God preferred Joseph and that their treatment of him was sinful; khatiʾ is deliberate error, while akhtaʾ is inadvertent error.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p274#2/r1.anchor: يقال: خطئ خطئا إذا تعمد، وأخطأ إذا كان غير متعمد

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r1.claim: The brothers acknowledge that God chose Joseph over them for his good appearance and complete conduct.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r1.anchor: اختارك علينا بحسن الصورة وكمال السيرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r2.claim: They admit that their conduct toward Joseph made them sinners.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:91/r2.anchor: إنا كنا مذنبين بما فعلنا معك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r1.claim: The Joseph story teaches patience, measured action, and entrusting matters to the Wise; difficult affairs unfold gradually as causes are ordered, testing both obedience and disobedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r1.anchor: على الاقتداء بأفعال الهداة المهديين في التأني والاتئاد وتفويض الأمور إلى الحكيم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r2.claim: The brothers confess God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, intellect, judgment, beauty, rule, piety, and other virtues; the shortened “in” heightens their urgent apology.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r2.anchor: فضلك علينا أي بالعلم والعقل والحكم والحسن والملك والتقوى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r3.claim: They call themselves intrinsically wrongdoers; “khaṭiʾīn” denotes deliberately committing sin.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p94/r3.anchor: أي عريقين في الخطأ , وهو تعمد الإثم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r1.claim: Qatadah says the brothers admitted God had favored Joseph over them and that they had encountered a forbearing man.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : قالوا تالله لقد اثرك الله علينا . وذلك بعدما عرفهم نفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq glosses أثرَك as God having favored Joseph over them.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r2.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق اثرك الله علينا اي : فضلك الله علينا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the brothers meant that they had done wrong in what they had done to Joseph.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2194/r3.anchor: عن ابن اسحاق : وان كنا لخاطئين اي : فيما صنعنا بك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r1.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r1.claim: The brothers say God preferred Joseph in kingship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r1.anchor: بالملك قاله الضحاك عن ابن عباس والثاني بالصبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r2.claim: They say God preferred Joseph for his patience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r2.anchor: بالصبر قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r3.claim: They say God preferred Joseph for his forbearance and forgiveness toward them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r3.anchor: بالحلم والصفح عنا ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r4.claim: A fourth interpretation includes Joseph’s knowledge, intelligence, beauty, and the other virtues he was given.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r4.anchor: بالعلم والعقل والحسن وسائر الفضائل التي أعطاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r5.claim: The brothers admit they were sinners and guilty regarding Joseph.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس لمذنبين آثمين في أمرك قال ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r6.claim: Khāṭiʾīn was chosen over mukhṭiʾīn because the former means sinful, while the latter means merely missing the right course without sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r6.anchor: معنى خطئ يخطأ فهو خاطئ آثم ومعنى أخطأ يخطئ فهو مخطئ ترك الصواب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r7.claim: The form khāṭiʾīn may also have been chosen to match the verse endings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون آثر خاطئين على مخطئين لموافقة رؤوس الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ gives two senses for in: “although we were sinners” or “we were only sinners.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p282/r8.anchor: وذكر الفراء في معنى إن قولين أحدهما وقد كنا خاطئين

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r10.claim: إيثار means preferring one thing over another and relates to choice and the lasting good impression behind أثر, آثار, and مأثرة.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r10.anchor: الإيثار: تفضيل أحد الشيئين على الآخر، ونظيره: الاختيار، والاجتباء نقيضه: الإيثار عليه

JISHUMI:v5p3709/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r11.claim: A خطيئة is moving something from its proper course; خطئ is deliberate misplacement, unlike أخطأ, which means to err or sin.
JISHUMI:v5p3709/r11.anchor: والخطيئة: إزالة الشيء عن جهته إلى ما لا يصلح فيه، خطئ خطأ فهو خاطئ

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r1.claim: خاطئين is accusative as the predicate of كان.

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r3.claim: Joseph's brothers say God chose and favored him over them in knowledge, judgment, and kingship.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r3.anchor: لقد آثرك الله علينا: اختارك وفضلك بالعلم والحكم والملك

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r4.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r4.claim: One explanation says they were mistaken in concealing Joseph's affair from their father.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r4.anchor: قيل: مخطئين في كتمان أمر يوسف لأبيهم، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r5.claim: Other glosses take خاطئين to mean sinners generally or wrongdoers against one another.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r5.anchor: وقيل: مذنبين، وقيل: خاطئين بيننا وبينك، عن الأصم.

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r6.claim: Abu Ali says the brothers began the wrongdoing in childhood but reached adulthood still concealing it from their father.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r6.anchor: قيل: إنهم ابتدؤوا الفعل وهم صبيان، وبلغوا مصرين على كتمان الأمر عن أبيهم يوهمون أن ما أخبروه على ما أخبروه، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r7.claim: Other explanations say they had to seek forgiveness after puberty, or that repentance was commendable though not obligatory and thus Joseph prayed for it.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r7.anchor: وقيل: كان يلزمهم الاستغفار بعد البلوغ، وقيل: التوبة وإن لم تجب فهو حسن، فلذلك استغفر لهم،

JISHUMI:v5p3710/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r8.claim: A further view says they were already adults but not prophets; the author prefers the view that they began as children and continued the concealment into adulthood.
JISHUMI:v5p3710/r8.anchor: وقيل: كانوا بالغين، ولم يكونوا أنبياء، والأول الوجه.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r1.claim: The brothers' admission that they were at fault refers to what they did to Joseph; it can mean either sinful or mistaken, with sinful implying culpability.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r1.anchor: أي فيما صنعوا بيوسف , وفيه قولان : أحدهما : آثمين . الثاني : مخطئين . والفرق بين الخاطئ والمخطئ أن الخاطئ آثم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r2.claim: Although the brothers were young when they first acted, they became culpable by growing up and continuing to conceal what they had done.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p75/r2.anchor: لما كبروا واستداموا إخفاء ما صنعوا صاروا حينئذ خاطئين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r1.claim: They acknowledge that God preferred Joseph over them through knowledge, forbearance, piety, patience, and beauty.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r1.anchor: اختارك وفضلك علينا بالعلم والحلم والتقوى والصبر والحسن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r2.claim: Their confession means they had deliberately sinned, neither practicing piety nor patience.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r2.anchor: أنا كنا خاطئين متعمدين للاثم لم نتق ولم نصبر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r3.claim: Joseph's kingship and their abasement as suppliants before him are the consequences of their wrongdoing.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p203#3/r3.anchor: لا جرم أن الله أعزك بالملك وأذلنا بالتمسكن بين يديك

MAJAZ:v1p317/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p317/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p317/r2.claim: وإن كنا لخاطئين means وإن كنا خاطئين; the added fatḥa-lām intensifies and confirms, and خطئت and أخطأت are equivalent.
MAJAZ:v1p317/r2.anchor: «وإن كنا لخاطئين» (91) مجازه: وإن كنا خاطئين، [وتزاد] اللام المفتوحة للتوكيد والتثبيت، وخطئت وأخطئت واحد

MAJAZ:v1p317/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p317/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
MAJAZ:v1p317/r3.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses خطئن to mean أخطأن.
MAJAZ:v1p317/r3.anchor: قال [امرؤ القيس] : يا لهف هند إذ خطئن كاهلا. أي أخطأن

MAJAZ:v1p317/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p317/r4.speaker: أمية بن الأسكر
MAJAZ:v1p317/r4.claim: Umayya ibn al-Askar’s line uses خطئا and حابا in the same sense of error.
MAJAZ:v1p317/r4.anchor: وقال: أمية بن الأسكر: وإن مهاجرين تكنفاه ... غداة إذ لقد خطئا وحابا

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r1.claim: Al-Asmaʿi explains “ātharaka” as God favoring Joseph; the phrase can also describe a servant whom someone prefers with special gifts.

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r2.claim: Joseph was favored over his brothers in knowledge, forbearance, reason, virtue, beauty, and kingship.
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r2.anchor: والمعنى : لقد فضلك الله علينا بالعلم

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r3.claim: Some infer that Joseph’s brothers were not prophets: prophethood outweighs worldly offices, so sharing that rank would make their confession of his superiority incoherent.
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r3.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بهذه الآية على أن إخوته ما كانوا أنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r4.claim: “Khāṭiʾ” denotes deliberate sin, unlike “mukhṭiʾ,” used for someone who strives to reach a legal judgment but errs.
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r4.anchor: قيل الخاطىء هو الذي أتى بالخطيئة عمدا وفرق بين الخاطىء والمخطىء

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r5.claim: Most commentators say the brothers apologize for throwing Joseph in the well, selling him, and separating him from their father.
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r5.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن الذي اعتذروا منه هو إقدامهم على إلقائه في الجب وبيعه

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r6.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r6.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi says they did not apologize for childhood acts before puberty, but for later hiding Joseph’s survival and failing to tell Jacob that the wolf had not eaten him.
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r6.anchor: وقال أبو علي الجبائي : إنهم لم يعتذروا إليه من ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p163/r7.claim: Razi rejects al-Jubbaʾi’s account as implausible: Jacob would hardly send unaccompanied prepubescent boys; even an unnecessary apology can still be fitting, as people may renew repentance after forgiveness.

STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.claim: Joseph’s no-reproach statement is called a beautiful form of forgiveness; reproach may also mean physical punishment.
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r1.anchor: There is no reproach against you this day is described in some sources as “a beautiful form of forgiveness”(Kl)

STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet cited Joseph’s forgiveness, then freed Quraysh after they acknowledged his noble status.
STUDYQURAN:12:91/r2.anchor: “Verily I say to you as Joseph said to his brothers: there is no reproach against you

TAB-FULL:v13p329/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r1.claim: Joseph’s brothers say God preferred him over them, granting him knowledge, forbearance, and virtue.
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r1.anchor: وقالوا: {تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين} [يوسف: 91] فيما كنا صنعنا بك

TAB-FULL:v13p329/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r2.claim: The brothers admit they wronged Joseph by separating him from his father and brother and through their other mistreatment.
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r2.anchor: وإن كنا لخاطئين} [يوسف: 91] فيما كنا صنعنا بك

TAB-FULL:v13p329/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r3.claim: خطئين means mistaken; the source distinguishes خطئَ يخطأ from أخطأ يخطئ and cites Umayya al-Askar’s verse as usage evidence.
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r3.anchor: إلا خاطئين: يعنون مخطئين، يقال منه: خطئ فلان يخطأ خطأ وخطأ، وأخطأ يخطئ إخطاء؛

TAB-FULL:v13p329/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r4.claim: The brothers apologize to Joseph for what they had done to him after he identifies himself.
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r4.anchor: عن أسباط، عن السدي، قال: " لما قال لهم يوسف: {أنا يوسف وهذا أخي} [يوسف: 90] اعتذروا إليه، وقالوا:

TAB-FULL:v13p329/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r5.claim: After Joseph identified himself, the brothers recognized that God had made him a forbearing man.
TAB-FULL:v13p329/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا} [يوسف: 91] وذلك بعد ما عرفهم أنفسهم، يقول: جعلك الله رجلا حليما

SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r1.claim: آثرك means ‘favored you’; إيثار is preferring someone in all kinds of gifts, from أثر, following a thing as though tracing every kind of honor.
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r1.anchor: أي: " تفضل عليك، والإيثار: التفضيل/ بجميع أنواع العطايا، آثره يؤثره إيثارا، وأصله من الأثر وهو تتبع الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r2.claim: The hadith ستكون بعدي أثرة means that some people will monopolize goods over others; استأثر means to reserve something for oneself, and God's استأثر بفلان figuratively means He chose him.
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r2.anchor:
وفي الحديث
" ستكون بعدي أثرة "
، أي: يستأثر بعضكم على بعض، ويقال: استأثر بكذا، أي: اختص به، واستأثر الله بفلان كناية عن اصطفائه،

SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r3.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses آثرك الله به إيثاراكا to attest God's granting special preference.
SAMIN-DURR:12:91/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: 2829 والله أسماك سما مباركا آثرك الله به إيثاركا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r1.claim: آثرتك means I preferred you; أثير describes someone specially favored and given preference.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r1.anchor: الأصمعي (¬2): آثرتك إيثارا، أي: فضلتك، وفلان أثير عند (¬3) فلان وذو أثره، إذا كان خاصا به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r2.claim: An athīr is someone whom another favors with special virtue and connection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r2.anchor: قال الليث: وهو الذي يؤثره بفضله وصلته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r3.claim: He glosses the confession as God having preferred Joseph over the brothers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬4): لقد فضلك الله علينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r4.claim: They specify Joseph's advantages as knowledge, forbearance, intelligence, virtue, beauty, and kingship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬5): أي بالعلم والحلم والعقل والفضل والحسن والملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses خاطئين as sinners; another reported gloss says they sinned against Joseph, meaning they were nothing but wrongdoers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬6): لمذنبين، وقال غيره: لآثمين في أمرك، والمعنى: وما كنا إلا خاطئين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r6.claim: خاطئين may mean مخطئين; al-Zajjaj chooses this sense, supported by the poetic use خطئن meaning أخطأن.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r6.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬7): ويجوز أن يكون (خاطئين) بمعنى: مخطئين، وهو اختيار الزجاج (¬8)، وأنشد (¬9):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r7.claim: The lexical distinction between خطئ and أخطأ was discussed at the verses about sin and inadvertent error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p236/r7.anchor: وذكرنا الكلام في: خطئ وأخطأ، عند قوله: {وأحاطت به خطيئته} [البقرة: 81]، وقوله: {إن نسينا أو أخطأنا} [البقر ة: 286].

QIRAAT-ER:12:91:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:91:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:91:13#1/r1.claim: A dialectal or Quranic variant simplifies and drops hamza in khāṭiʾīna, without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:12:91:13#1/r1.anchor: Drops hamzah from khāṭiʾīna → khāṭīna; dialectal/Quranic variant; the hamzah is simplified

ITQAN:v2p499/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.claim: The non-governing lām of initiation emphasizes a clause and shifts away from sentence-initial position after inna to avoid two successive emphatics; it also makes the imperfect refer to the present.
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.anchor: لام الابتداء وفائدتها أمران توكيد مضمون الجملة ولهذا زحلقوها في باب إن عن صدر الجملة

ITQAN:v2p499/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r4.claim: The lām of an oath’s response, or of law and lawla, appears in the examples cited; the target verse’s لقد آثرك الله is an oath response.
ITQAN:v2p499/r4.anchor: ولام الجواب للقسم أو لو أو لولا نحو ﴿ تالله لقد آثرك الله ﴾

ITQAN:v4p328/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.claim: Al-Barizi says eloquence chooses the most fitting words for each part of a sentence; humans cannot usually summon every meaning and matching expression, while this is present in God’s knowledge, making the Quran the finest and most eloquent speech.
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.anchor: قال البارزي في أول كتابه ( أنوار التحصيل في أسرار التنزيل ) اعلم أن المعنى الواحد قد يخبر عنه

ITQAN:v4p328/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.claim: Al-Barizi illustrates preference for lighter diction with آمن over صدق, آثرك الله over فضلك, أتى over أعطى, أنذر over خوف, خير لكم over أفضل لكم, and shorter nominal forms and تنكح.
ITQAN:v4p328/r6.anchor: و ﴿ آثرك ﴾ ﴿ الله ﴾ أخف من ( فضلك ) و ﴿ أتى ﴾ أخف من ( أعطى )

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r1.claim: Tāʾ is an oath particle restricted to the name Allah; it occurs five times in the Qur’an, three in Joseph and twice in al-Naḥl.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r1.anchor: التاء حرف قسم مثل الواو لكن التاء تكون مختصّة بلفظ الجلالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r2.claim: Tāʾ in this oath conveys veneration and is etymologically a substitution for wāw, which is commonly used to swear by other things such as dawn, forenoon, night, and sun.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p638/r2.anchor: والتاء في أصلها اللغوي مُبدلةٌ من الواو

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.claim: Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2.anchor: هم لم يسألوه المغفرة وإنما هو الذي دعا لهم بالمغفرة دون أن يسألوه حتى أنهم لم يذكروا الخطيئة التي ارتكبوها بحق يوسف
